thread:
Maria Chen: Hey team — acme-inc is hitting intermittent failures on /v1/embeddings and sometimes when reranking. They surface as a shape/dim mismatch downstream. Happened ~2025-11-12 14:03 UTC. Customer says they didn’t change client code. Request IDs: req_01a2b3c4, req_01a2b3c5, req_01a2b3d0. Can someone triage?

Daniel Park: Can you paste one of the failing request payloads and a curl repro? Also which model exactly (catalog name + pinned version)?

Maria Chen: Model is open-embed-large-v2@v2025-10-09. Repro curl (sanitized):

```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \  --data '{"model":"open-embed-large-v2","input":[[0.1,0.2,...(1536 floats omitted)...], [0.05,0.01,...(1024 floats omitted)...]]}'
```
Customer payload was batching mixed-length vectors (some 1536, some 1024). Server error in logs: `BatchValidationError: batch contains vectors with inconsistent dimensions (expected 1536, got 1024)`. But that only shows up for a subset of requests — others with same client library succeed.

Ashley Rivera: Do we know if their client is gzipping or chunking the JSON? Mixed batches could come from a client-side aggregation bug. Any signs of gzip header mismatch or Content-Encoding in the request logs?

Maria Chen: Customer said they use our JS SDK with default batching enabled. They don't gzip. They also reported intermittent 429s in the same timeframe. I grabbed raw request headers from one ID: `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`, `User-Agent: acme-search/2.1.0`, no Content-Encoding.

Daniel Park: Okay. Two-pronged ask for triage: 1) attempt local curl repro copying the payload exactly, 2) capture service-side request + routing logs for those request IDs and upload a debug bundle. I can try (1) now if someone uploads the exact payload (not sanitized).

Maria Chen: Uploading a redacted-but-reproducible sample now to the debug channel. Here's a minimized failing payload that reproduces the dimension error (vector values truncated):

```
{
  "model": "open-embed-large-v2",
  "input": [
    [0.001, 0.002, /* ... total 1536 floats ... */],
    [0.003, 0.004 /* ... only 1024 floats ... */]
  ]
}
```

Support Bot: To collect a debug bundle for these request IDs, run:

```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $SUPPORT_KEY" \  -X POST "https://internal.redwood.ai/support/debug-bundle" \  -d '{"request_ids":["req_01a2b3c4","req_01a2b3c5","req_01a2b3d0"],"include_routes":true,"include_raw_body":true}'
```

Support Bot: Uploaded bundle placeholder: https://internal.redwood.ai/debug/UPLOAD-PLACEHOLDER-1769991234 (replace with real upload token when run).

SRE Bot: Automated check: these request IDs passed through edge-node-eu-7 and then routed to inference-pool-3. Edge logs show a 502 for req_01a2b3c5 at 14:04:12 UTC with backend error: `InvalidBatch: inconsistent vector dims`. No evidence of gzip/transfer-encoding mismatches at edge.

Ashley Rivera: If edge consistently sees consistent dims but backend reports mixed dims, possibilities: 1) client-side batching aggregator concatenating two prior queued payloads (race), 2) request deserialization bug in the batching layer, or 3) malformed JSON due to charset issues. Can customer reproduce with batching disabled?

Maria Chen: I asked customer to disable client-side batching and retest (they’re running a hotfix now). They also agreed to run a curl using the explicit batch array (I gave the simplified payload above).

Daniel Park: I ran the curl (using the simplified payload). On my machine I can't reproduce the error sending a single request. Trying a tight loop of two back-to-back POSTs now to simulate aggregator race.

Daniel Park: Update — after sending two rapid POSTs with different vector lengths via a small node script hitting our API through the SDK, I see one failure that matches `BatchValidationError: inconsistent dims` when requests were routed to inference-pool-3. Repro seems tied to concurrent small requests hitting the same worker during a scaling event.

Ashley Rivera: Good find. Next steps: 1) collect full debug bundle from edge and worker for the failing request IDs (Maria please upload when available), 2) reproduce on a staging cluster that mirrors scaling events, 3) add defensive validation in batching layer to reject mixed-dim batches earlier and return 400 instead of 500/502.

Maria Chen: Uploading the full bundle now (link: https://internal.redwood.ai/debug/1769991234/bundle.tgz). Also adding customer-provided tcpdump and SDK logs to the bundle.

Support Bot: Bundle received. Ticketing note added to ACME-4578 and assigning to eng-runtime.

Ashley Rivera: I'll open a runtime PR with a quick guard for the batching aggregator. Daniel — can you add your repro script to the debug bundle so we can run in CI?

Daniel Park: Yeah dropping the repro script into the bundle in 10m.

Maria Chen: Thanks everyone. I’ll keep the customer updated: we’ve reproduced a race-related mixed-dim batch, collecting bundles and will patch the batching guard. Will follow up in this thread once the fix is deployed. :thumbsup:

Ashley Rivera: :eyes: pinging eng-runtime to prioritize.
